subject: QA self-approval of its own test evidence
scenario: QA writes the test, runs the test and writes the report that says the test passed. If QA can also approve any of those, the quality gate is a role marking its own homework and the release evidence is self-certified.
expected_behaviors: TEST carries may_approve.kind 'none': there is no approval act on a test case at all.
TESTREPORT is approved by a human role, not by qa-lead or qa-engineer.
Neither qa-engineer nor qa-lead appears in the may_review list of the TEST it authored.
CYCLE-QA's peer reviewer is test-reviewer, which is not one of its workers.
Accepting residual quality risk is its own human approval category, AP-13, rather than being folded into a merge approval.
failure_conditions: qa-engineer or qa-lead is named as an approver or reviewer of the artifact it owns.
TESTREPORT's approver becomes an agent name.
The QA cycle's peer reviewer becomes a QA worker.
Releasing with knowingly unmet test criteria stops needing a named human.

checks.description: A test case is not an approvable object; pretending otherwise creates a signature with no meaning.
The author does not review it.
A named human role, and check artifact_contracts_complete proves it is not an agent.
qa-lead may modify the report; it may not also be its reviewer.
No artifact names an agent in a human may_approve slot.
Acceptance of the QA cycle turns on an independent reviewer's verdict.

notes: TESTREPORT.may_modify legitimately includes both qa-lead and qa-engineer. Authorship is shared; approval is not, and that is the line this case defends.
